title.text: Matt Pocock Skills: Daily Developer Guide
picker.label: Language
hero.title: How to use these skills in actual daily dev work
hero.intro1: This guide is not a repo summary. It is a practical operating manual for using the skills as a software developer: shaping a feature, fixing a bug, spinning up a prototype, writing tests, understanding an unfamiliar codebase, and keeping work ready for async agent execution.
hero.intro2: Core frame: treat the agent as a junior engineer with weird constraints, not smart autocomplete. The skills encode the senior-engineer habits that keep that junior productive — slow down, build context, write one test at a time, then zoom back out.
hero.flow3: Use the workflow recipe that matches your task.
hero.flow4: Prefer small vertical slices over big all-at-once implementation.

mentalModel.heading: Mental Model
mentalModel.prototype.html: Prototype: answer a question with throwaway code.
mentalModel.prdIssues.html: PRD / Issues: turn decisions into executable work.
mentalModel.tddDiagnose.html: TDD / Diagnose: use feedback loops instead of guessing.
mentalModel.zoomOut.html: Zoom Out: understand system shape before changing it.
caveats.heading: Caveats
caveats.stackBias.html: Stack bias: skills lean TypeScript / Node + GitHub issues. Django, GitLab, or other setups may need a forked skill.
caveats.modelStrength.html: Model strength: grilling skills can bail or refuse on smaller / non-frontier models. Use Claude or GPT frontier tiers for best results.
caveats.installLean.html: Install lean: only enable the skills you'll actually use. A bloated skill set hurts the agent's intent matching.
start.heading: Start Here
start.intro: The repo is designed around small composable skills, but there is still one setup step you should not skip.
start.install.heading: 1. Install
start.install.body.html: Add the pack with npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills, then select the skills you want and make sure /setup-matt-pocock-skills is included.
start.configure.heading: 2. Configure Per Repo
start.configure.body.html: Run /setup-matt-pocock-skills once. It records your issue tracker, triage labels, and whether the repo has one global domain context or multiple.
start.callout1: If you skip setup, the planning and issue skills lose context about where tickets live and how the repo documents domain language and architecture.
start.callout2.html: Missing symlink after install? The installer drops everything into .agents/ (with skills/ inside), but Claude Code only looks at .claude/. The fix is a single directory-level symlink: .claude → .agents, so opening .claude shows the same skills/ folder. On fresh repos that link sometimes doesn't get created, so /setup-matt-pocock-skills and friends are silently missing. Verify with ls -la .claude — if it isn't a symlink to .agents, create it manually and restart Claude Code so the registry reloads.
start.install1.heading.html: Option A · Manual install run in your shell
start.install1.intro.html: Install the pack yourself, then make sure the .claude → .agents symlink is in place so Claude Code can see the skills.
start.install2.heading.html: Option B · Install by prompt paste into Claude Code
start.install2.intro: Prefer to let the agent drive? Paste this in and it will install the pack, fix the symlink if needed, then run setup with you.
start.install2.label: Paste into your agent
